stories.title: First-run project-init guidance without mutation
stories.observable_contract: Pi starts in a fresh project and explains project-init guidance before any apply or recovery mutation.
stories.technical_contract: The shim/helper reads project-local state, offers a plan-first path, and preserves no-mutation evidence until explicit approval.

stories.title: Initialized project imports approved ContextForge tools
stories.observable_contract: Pi shows approved ContextForge-backed tools after initialization in an ordinary session.
stories.technical_contract: The Pi adapter imports only approved services from project state and routes them through the ContextForge wrapper.

stories.title: Select, decline, and defer ContextForge services
stories.observable_contract: The user can select, decline, or defer service activation choices and see the result clearly.
stories.technical_contract: The helper records explicit choices without silently promoting unchosen services.

stories.title: Scoped consent plan approval and apply
stories.observable_contract: The user sees a scoped plan, approves it, and Pi reports only the approved apply result.
stories.technical_contract: Consent receipts bind plan digest, challenge, approval, and apply scope before state mutation.

stories.title: Safe governance read through ContextForge tool
stories.observable_contract: The user asks Pi about project governance and gets a safe read-only answer through a ContextForge tool.
stories.technical_contract: The ContextForge route exposes read-only governance data with no ledger mutation or secret leakage.

stories.title: Repairable service import failure with plan-first recovery
stories.observable_contract: A failed service import is explained with a repair plan instead of being hidden or half-applied.
stories.technical_contract: The helper classifies the failure, preserves current state, and produces a bounded recovery proposal.

stories.title: Authenticated route without token exposure
stories.observable_contract: The user sees an authenticated ContextForge tool work without seeing bearer tokens or secret values.
stories.technical_contract: The wrapper and Pi shim pass scoped credentials through redacted environment or cache paths only.

stories.title: Reload boundary after shim install or update
stories.observable_contract: After a shim install or update, Pi clearly indicates that a reload is required before relying on new behavior.
stories.technical_contract: Install/update state is separate from live-session readiness and requires explicit Pi reload evidence.

stories.title: Multi-turn plan persistence and stale digest rejection
stories.observable_contract: The user can continue a plan across turns, but stale approval input is rejected with a clear explanation.
stories.technical_contract: Plan cache, challenge id, and digest must match before apply can proceed.

stories.title: Helper and shim state readback for current project
stories.observable_contract: The user can ask Pi what ContextForge state it is using for the current project.
stories.technical_contract: Readback reports current project root, imported services, tool names, skips, and bounded errors.

stories.title: Capability discovery with ContextForge as authority
stories.observable_contract: The user asks what capabilities are available and Pi answers from ContextForge-backed authority.
stories.technical_contract: Capability discovery flows through project state and ContextForge readback, not stale client-local assumptions.

stories.title: Service onboarding handoff for uncataloged capability
stories.observable_contract: When the user asks for an uncataloged capability, Pi offers an onboarding handoff instead of pretending it exists.
stories.technical_contract: The helper creates a service-onboarding path with classification, feasibility, and implementation footprint planning.

stories.title: Project-root safety refusal for broad or unsafe roots
stories.observable_contract: Pi refuses or defers activation when the working directory is too broad or unsafe.
stories.technical_contract: Project-root inspection enforces configured root boundaries before helper planning or tool import.

stories.title: Dev Docker baseline session imports mentality tools
stories.observable_contract: A Pi dev Docker baseline session imports and can see the expected mentality tools.
stories.technical_contract: The client harness starts Pi against ContextForge dev Docker and exposes the project-local mentality route.

stories.title: Manual validation choice when safe probe is unavailable
stories.observable_contract: If no safe automated probe exists, Pi tells the user that manual validation is required.
stories.technical_contract: Validation policy distinguishes safe probes, conditional probes, skipped probes, and manual proof requirements.

stories.title: Layered readiness answer without collapsed claims
stories.observable_contract: Pi reports readiness by layer instead of saying generic done, ready, or validated.
stories.technical_contract: Readiness answers use the project vocabulary and cite missing stronger layers.

stories.title: Dev gateway unreachable at session start
stories.observable_contract: Pi starts, detects that the dev gateway is unreachable, and gives a bounded recovery path.
stories.technical_contract: Startup checks classify ContextForge dev Docker reachability separately from Pi shim load failure.

stories.title: Corrupt project-state file blocks activation safely
stories.observable_contract: Pi refuses activation when project state is corrupt and explains the repair boundary.
stories.technical_contract: Project-state parsing fails closed, preserves the file, and reports schema or JSON errors without apply mutation.

stories.title: ContextForge server id drift rebind
stories.observable_contract: Pi notices that the stored server id no longer matches ContextForge and offers a rebind path.
stories.technical_contract: Registry readback detects server-id drift and distinguishes rebind planning from unapproved registry mutation.

stories.title: Scoped token expires during interaction
stories.observable_contract: When a scoped token expires, Pi reports auth expiry and prompts for a safe refresh path.
stories.technical_contract: Wrapper errors classify token expiry, redact token material, and avoid silent fallback to broader credentials.

stories.title: Unsafe tool request redirected to safe path
stories.observable_contract: A risky tool request is refused or redirected to a safe read-only or plan-first alternative.
stories.technical_contract: Tool policy gates distinguish safe calls, conditional calls, and approval-required mutation paths.

stories.title: Wrapper crash produces bounded diagnostics
stories.observable_contract: If a wrapper crashes, Pi shows a concise diagnostic instead of dumping noisy stderr or hanging.
stories.technical_contract: The wrapper captures bounded stderr tails, exit class, and recovery hints without leaking secrets.

stories.title: Project root changes mid-session
stories.observable_contract: If the user changes project roots mid-session, Pi detects the mismatch before using stale tools.
stories.technical_contract: Session state binds the project root and invalidates or refreshes tool routes when the root changes.

stories.title: Concurrent session stale plan conflict
stories.observable_contract: Two Pi sessions cannot apply the same stale plan without a clear conflict message.
stories.technical_contract: Plan/apply state uses digests, timestamps, or journals to reject stale concurrent applies.

stories.title: Interrupted apply resumes through recovery journal
stories.observable_contract: After an interrupted apply, Pi can explain what happened and offer journal-based recovery.
stories.technical_contract: Apply operations write enough recovery journal evidence to classify complete, partial, and rollback-needed states.

stories.title: User asks for absent tool and Pi admits gap
stories.observable_contract: When the user asks for a missing tool, Pi admits the gap and offers the next useful path.
stories.technical_contract: Tool guidance maps absent capability to discovery, onboarding, or explicit unsupported status without hallucinating availability.
